researched.name: Resonance Specialties Ltd
researched.reason: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 34.29 cr (+59.2% YoY) and PAT Rs 8.47 cr (+411.0%), PBT margin 10.8% -> 32.9%, with H1 PAT of Rs 14.21 cr already above the whole of FY26's Rs 10.40 cr - at 11.97x trailing on BSE's own header (EPS 18.47, PB 4.26, ROE 35.61) and a Rs 255.1 cr market cap, debt-free at 30-Sep-2026 with 41-day receivables and H1 operating cash flow of Rs 13.02 cr against PAT of Rs 14.21 cr. Published at MEDIUM confidence because the research produced a mechanism AND a warning, and both are on the card. The mechanism: conversion charges - work put out to a third party - fell 27.5% in absolute rupees (Q2 Rs 4.64 cr -> Rs 3.36 cr, 21.5% -> 9.8% of sales) while revenue rose 59.2%, with materials flat at ~39.5%, so the margin is operating leverage plus in-housing, not a one-off; and exports did it, Rs 49.31 cr in H1 against Rs 22.75 cr (+116.8%, now 73.7% of revenue) while domestic sales FELL 12.4%. The FY26 report states how: 'Successful distillation of Crudes into value added FG products from new import source. The cost of products derived is halved than synthetic route.' The warning is the volume arithmetic, which is the single best thing this run found and comes from the company's own Form A energy disclosure: production of pyridines/lutidines/collidines/cyanopyridines backs out three independent ways (HSD, coal, electricity) to 533-542 MT in FY26 against 541-545 MT in FY25 - FLAT - while revenue rose 16.0%, so FY26's growth was realisation (Rs 14.38 -> Rs 16.68 lakh per MT) and not tonnes. Whether H1 FY27 is tonnes or price is UNKNOWN until the FY27 annual report publishes Form A, and that is stated as the card's first unknown. And the related-party cluster, every line of it from the company's own notes: 100% of FY26 conversion charges, Rs 16.78 cr or 18.6% of revenue, went to Kaygee Laboratories Pvt Ltd, a promoter-group company; the advance against supplies to Kaygee rose from Rs 0.83 cr to Rs 2.75 cr with interest booked on it; and on 4-Aug-2026 the board approved buying Kaygee's Mandideep plant on a slump-sale basis for Rs 29.98 cr cash by 30-Nov-2026 - 1.79x that annual job-work billing - against Rs 20.67 cr of cash and mutual funds at 30-Sep and only Rs 14 cr of CRISIL BBB-/Stable bank lines, with NO disclosed funding plan. The resolution, being a material related-party transaction from which the 54.25% promoters had to abstain, passed on 18-Sep-2026 on 37,867 valid votes - 0.33% of capital and about 0.72% of the public float. Two further honest marks against it: market cap of Rs 255.1 cr sits BELOW the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where every 5x run of the last three years clustered, and today's close of Rs 221.00 is the 52-week high after +128.1% in a year on 17.4x median volume, which our own study says is an alarm bell and not evidence. Management gives no guidance of any kind - no presentation, no call, no NSE listing - and the card says so in the guidance field with the eleven documents read to establish it.

researched.name: Camlin Fine Sciences Ltd
researched.verdict: NOT PUBLISHED - and the scan's trigger was a MISCLASSIFICATION
researched.reason: The scan scored this 6.0 with {'ORDER': 1, 'VOL': 1}. The filing was opened, and it is NOT an order. It is the Reg 30 disclosure of 30-Oct-2026 17:07 that the company has received an ADMINISTRATIVE WARNING LETTER FROM SEBI (ref I/24675/2026 dated 29-Oct-2026, received by courier 30-Oct). The letter, which is attached in full and was read: for the quarters from 30-Jun-2016 to 31-Mar-2023 the company classified Ms Radha Pandit (spouse of promoter Mr Ashish Dandekar) and Mr Anand Pandit (her father) as PUBLIC shareholders instead of promoter group, violating Regulations 31(1) and 31(4) read with 4(1)(c) and 4(1)(e) of the LODR; SEBI says the violation 'has been viewed seriously' and warns the company and its board to improve compliance standards 'failing which appropriate enforcement action may be initiated'. The company says it has since revised the filings retrospectively and that there is no financial impact. So the day's news here is a governance red flag with no number attached, not an operational trigger: there is no order, no capex, no rating action and no result. Not researched further and not published. FOR THE OWNER - this is a scan.py defect worth fixing: the subject line is the generic 'Announcement Under Regulation 30 SEBI (LODR) Regulations - Receipt Of SEBI Administrative Warning Letter', so the filing went to the body-text classifier, and the body contains the Reg 30 table row 'Nature and details of the action(s) taken or order(s) passed'. The word 'order' in that boilerplate is what produced an ORDER category. Every SEBI/regulatory-action filing in the market carries that exact phrase, so this will recur daily until the ORDER-from-body-text rule excludes it.

FILINGS carried the day. Four names were taken to a verdict and one was published. Resonance Specialties is a Rs 255 cr pyridine maker whose Q2 revenue rose 59.2% and PBT margin went from 10.8% to 32.9%, and the interesting work was not the headline but two things underneath it. First, the cost line: conversion charges - work put out - fell 27.5% in rupees while revenue rose 59.2%, and the FY26 notes show every rupee of those charges goes to Kaygee Laboratories, a promoter-group company whose plant the board agreed on 4-Aug to buy for Rs 29.98 cr cash by 30-Nov, against Rs 20.67 cr of liquidity and Rs 14 cr of rated bank lines, with no funding plan disclosed and a related-party mandate carried on 37,867 votes, 0.33% of the capital. Second, the volume arithmetic: the company publishes no capacity, but its Form A energy disclosure backs out production three independent ways to ~540 MT in both FY26 and FY25, so FY26's 16% revenue growth was entirely realisation. That single derived fact is what turns a 12x re-rating story into a medium-confidence one, and it is on the card.

The other three verdicts were worth the time for a different reason. Camlin Fine Sciences scored as an ORDER and turned out to be a SEBI administrative warning letter for misclassifying two promoter-group persons as public shareholders across 27 quarters - and the misclassification is traceable to one line of Reg 30 boilerplate, 'the action(s) taken or order(s) passed', which will mis-score every regulatory-action filing in the market until it is excluded. Regency Fincorp's top-equal score of 8.0 came from a rating REAFFIRMATION and two routine NBFC debenture allotments. Pune E-Stock Broking posted a genuinely good half but has no physical driver this method can model.

THE PYTHON-INTERPRETER TRAP RECURRED FOR A THIRD RUN AND WAS CAUGHT BEFORE ANY BUILDER RAN. Step 0 of the routine prompt says `pip install --quiet pymupdf`, but on this VM `pip` belongs to python3.13 while the interpreter that runs the builders is python3.11.17. The install 'succeeded' and `import fitz` still failed. It was fixed with `python3 -m pip install pymupdf xlrd` BEFORE scan.py or minsteel.py ran, which is why scan.py printed SELFTEST PASS first time and no empty files were written into the PDF-text cache - unlike 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-29, when the same trap produced a SELFTEST FAIL and 77 poisoned cache entries. SUGGESTED FIX, now three runs old: change step 0 of the routine prompt from `pip install` to `python3 -m pip install`.

scan.py MISCLASSIFIES EVERY REGULATORY-ACTION FILING AS AN ORDER WIN. Camlin Fine Sciences (532834) scored 6.0 today with {'ORDER': 1}; the filing is SEBI's administrative warning letter of 29-Oct-2026 over shareholding-pattern misclassification. The subject is the generic 'Announcement Under Regulation 30 SEBI (LODR) Regulations - Receipt Of SEBI Administrative Warning Letter', so the filing goes to the body-text classifier, and the body carries the mandatory Reg 30 table row 'Nature and details of the action(s) taken or order(s) passed'. That boilerplate 'order(s) passed' is what produces the ORDER category. Every SEBI, DGTR, tax and court action filing in the market carries the same phrase, so this recurs daily and inflates the candidate list with governance bad news scored as order wins. Yesterday's run hit the same class of defect from the other side (a High Court stay on rescinded contracts scored as an order). The owner owns scan.py; the fix is to exclude that phrase from the ORDER-from-body-text rule.
